title: Unity
sub: The main thread, UnitySynchronizationContext and Awaitable
cards/0/body: Almost the entire Unity API (transform, GameObject, components) works only from the main thread. Unity installs its own UnitySynchronizationContext: the continuation after await runs on the main thread, in the next frame.
cards/1/task: The script moves a transform after await. Run it as is.
cards/2/explain: ConfigureAwait(false) sent the continuation to the pool, and you can't touch a transform from there.
cards/3/task: Fix it: the continuation must return to the main thread.
cards/4/task: Unity can hang too. Drive it into a deadlock.
cards/5/body: Since Unity 2023.1 (and in Unity 6) there's an Awaitable class: cheap waits with no extra allocations.
cards/5/deep: Awaitable objects come from a pool and go back to it when they complete. So you can't await the same Awaitable twice: the second await may get someone else's operation. If you need to await several times, wrap it in a Task.
cards/6/q: Compute in the background, then move the object
cards/6/explain: Without MainThreadAsync, the transform line will throw.
cards/8/q: Can you await the same Awaitable twice?
cards/8/options/0: No: the Awaitable goes back to the pool, and a second await is unpredictable
cards/8/options/2: Yes, but only on the main thread
cards/8/explain: That's the price of zero allocations.
